shape_raw: metallic gold/bronze elongated disk-like object with bright white/blue radiant glare on one end
summary: Composite sketch dated 30 April 2024 depicts a metallic disk-shaped object with intense white/blue light emission hovering above a tree line in open grassland.

location_text: vicinity Dijon, France (return from night mission to Luxeuil)
shape_raw: very bright glow
witness_role: French Air Force aircrew (Mirage IV pilot and navigator)
summary: Mirage IV crew (P: Herve Giraud, with navigator) at Mach 0.9 / 9,600 m observed a very bright glow at 3 o'clock on collision course. Two engagements: glow followed the Mirage at constant 1,500-2,000 m even through 6.5 g banks, then disappeared. Contrexeville military radar had no contact; controller suggested an oxygen problem.
outcome: Returned safely to Luxeuil; no radar contact; cause unknown.

location_text: Rennes-Nantes-Poitiers itinerary, France (en route to Tours)
shape_raw: sphere 1-2 m diameter with tail like a comet, fluorescent green, magnesium-fire-type center
witness_role: French Air Force student pilot (T-33, Col. Claude Bosc)
summary: Student pilot at 6,000 m and 460 km/h saw what he first took for a green flare which exceeded his altitude by 1,500 m, then approached on collision course filling his windshield. Sphere with fluorescent green tail passed grazing his right wing in under 5 seconds. Two trailing pilots saw it from a distance; ground radar had no contact.
outcome: No collision; pilot landed safely; corroborated by trailing aircraft.

location_text: vicinity Coulommiers, Seine-et-Marne, France (Nice-London leg of AF 3532)
shape_raw: brown bell, then chestnut-brown lens, ~250 m long
witness_role: Air France airline crew (captain Jean-Charles Duboc, copilot Valerie Chauffour, chief steward)
summary: Air France flight AF 3532 cruising at 11,900 m observed a large brown bell-shaped craft at ~10,500 m and 50 km, which morphed to a lens shape and disappeared instantaneously on the aircraft's left side. Cinq-Mars-la-Pile control center recorded a 50-second radar track crossing AF 3532's path with no filed flight plan; weather-balloon hypothesis ruled out by CODA. CRNA-North investigated only three such cases in seven years (3,000 movements/day).
outcome: Airmiss procedure followed on landing; balloon hypothesis ruled out by CODA.

location_text: RAF Lakenheath / Bentwaters, ~30 km NE of Cambridge, UK
shape_raw: bright light, multiple radar tracks; one stationary, one transiting at 2000-4000 mph
witness_role: USAF/RAF radar controllers, control tower, military transport pilot, RAF Venom interceptor crew
summary: Multiple-witness radar/visual case at joint USAF-RAF Lakenheath-Bentwaters. Object transited base east-to-west at 2,000-4,000 mph, others jumped from immobility to 600-950 km/h with no transition, made line-segment moves with abrupt 3-6 minute stops. RAF Venom night fighter locked machine guns on target which then maneuvered behind the fighter and trailed it. Listed "unidentified" in Condon Report.
outcome: Object departed northbound at 950 km/h at 0330 hrs; Condon classified unidentified.

location_text: Mississippi / Louisiana / Texas (Gulf Coast region), USA
shape_raw: intense bluish-white light, large red light
witness_role: USAF aircrew (RB-47 ECM-equipped bomber: pilot Cmdr. Chase, copilot Capt. MacCoyd, ECM officers MacClure and Provenzano, navigator)
summary: RB-47 reconnaissance bomber at Mach 0.75 detected pulsed-microwave source (~3000 MHz, 2 us pulses) circling the aircraft, followed by visual contact with a bluish-white light then large red light maintaining 18 km constant distance. Object simultaneously disappeared from RB-47 onboard radar, ground 'Utah' radar, and MacClure's ECM scope west of Dallas, then reappeared. Listed "unidentified" in Condon Report.
outcome: Multi-evidence chase across three states; classified unidentified.

location_text: Gemini 7 spacecraft, low Earth orbit, approximately 4 hr 24 min into flight
shape_raw: a bogey at ten o'clock high
summary: Gemini 7 CDR Borman called out a 'bogey at ten o'clock high' to Houston as a sighting separate from the spent booster and accompanying particle field. Borman re-confirmed it was an actual sighting in addition to the booster (which he and CMP Lovell also had in sight) and a particle stream three to four miles to the left. PAO commentary characterized the third object as a 'bogey'.
outcome: Sighting recorded on PAO release tape; no resolution stated in transcript.

location_text: vicinity Erstein (V-9381), France
shape_raw: large red light at 2000 ft going East at 18:40 hrs. Travelling at approximately 200 MPH
summary: Night of 14-15 December 1944. 415 NFS aircraft flying at 1000 ft observed a large red light at 2000 ft going east at ~200 MPH near Erstein.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: 20 miles north of Breisach (W-0173), Germany
shape_raw: 5 or 6 flashing red and green lights in 'T' shape
summary: Night of 16-17 December 1944. 415 NFS observed 5-6 flashing red and green lights in a 'T' shape at 800 ft. Initially thought to be flak; about 10 minutes later same lights closed in to 8 o'clock position at 1000 ft and remained for several minutes before disappearing. Aircraft turned port and starboard and lights followed.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: patrolling Sarrebourg to Strasbourg, vicinity Nagenau, France
shape_raw: two lights coming towards A/C from the ground; appeared to be a large orange glow
summary: Night of 22-23 December 1944. Patrolling Angels 10 from Sarrebourg to Strasbourg. At 06:00 hrs saw two lights climb from the ground, level off at the aircraft's altitude, sit on tail for about 2 minutes as a large orange glow, then peel off, fly level for a few minutes and go out. Appeared under perfect control.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: European theater (location unspecified)
shape_raw: reddish colored flames at considerable distance
summary: Night of 23-24 December 1944. 415 NFS observed reddish colored flames at considerable distance, approximately 10,000 ft.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: approximately 10 miles south of Point X (Q6745)
shape_raw: glowing red object shooting straight up
summary: Night of 23-24 December 1944. ~10 miles south of Point X, observer noticed approximately 5 miles to NE a glowing red object shooting straight up. It changed suddenly to plane view of A/C doing a wing-over and going into a dive and disappearing.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: vicinity Q-9050 / R-1556
shape_raw: two yellow streaks of flame; red balls of fire that stayed up for 10 seconds approximately 45 miles away; groups of lights making distinct lines somewhat like arrows
summary: Night of 26-27 December 1944, 01:45 hrs. Two yellow streaks of flame at ~3000 ft off port side; also red balls of fire ~45 miles away staying up for 10 seconds. Felt prop-wash. Several groups of lights off port observed near Q-9050 and R-1556 making distinct arrow-like lines. GCI Blunder: no enemy aircraft in area.
outcome: Unexplained; GCI confirmed no E/A

location_text: vector 090 near V-7050
shape_raw: airborne white lights, staggered evenly vertically, 1 to 4 swing at once, appeared stationary
summary: Night of 26-27 December 1944. While on vector 090 near V-7050, observed airborne white lights staggered evenly vertically; could see 1 to 4 swing at once; appeared stationary at 10,000 ft.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: vicinity Worms, Germany
shape_raw: light at same altitude
summary: Night of 26-27 December 1944. Observer near Worms saw a light at same altitude come within 100 ft. Aircraft peeled off and took evasive action but light continued to follow for 5 minutes; light then pulled up rapidly and went out of sight.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: vicinity Q-1378
shape_raw: lights suspended in air moving slowly and would then disappear; orange in color; observed singly and in pairs
summary: Night of 27-28 December 1944. While on north heading in patrol area, noticed in vicinity of Q-1378 lights suspended in air moving slowly and then disappearing — orange in color, singly and in pairs. Observed four or five times during period.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: 8 miles NE of Luneville, France
shape_raw: three sets of three lights (red and white), one on starboard and one on port
summary: Night of 27-28 December 1944, 19:10 hrs. 8 miles NE of Luneville saw three sets of three lights (red and white), one on starboard and one on port closing from 1000 ft to 2000 ft to rear at Angels 10. Pulled up to Angels 8 and lights went out. Called Churchman — negative reply.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: 30-40 miles east of base
shape_raw: a group of lights flying through the air
summary: Night of 30-31 December 1944. Saw a group of lights flying through the air 30-40 miles east of base while flying at Angels 9-10.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: vicinity Ingweiler
shape_raw: large orange glow in sky approx. 5 ft. in diameter
summary: Night of 14-15 January 1945, 20:00 hrs. Observed a large orange glow in the sky approximately 5 ft in diameter at 6,000 ft, vicinity Ingweiler.
outcome: Unexplained

location_text: between Weissembourg and Landau
shape_raw: Foofighter — amber lights, one 20-50 ft above the other, about 1 ft in diameter, ~30 seconds duration
summary: Night of 29-30 January 1945, 00:10 hrs. Sighted a Foofighter about halfway between Weissembourg and Landau. Off starboard rear at Angels 2. Amber lights staggered 20-50 ft apart vertically; ~30 second duration; ~1 ft diameter; ~1000 ft away following. Lights disappeared when Travel 34 turned into them.
outcome: Unexplained — Foofighter

location_text: vicinity F-5710 (European theater)
shape_raw: aluminum colored cylinder shaped object, about 12 ft long and 1 ft in diameter, suspended vertically with small fins and a mast projecting from the lower end
summary: 1 March 1945, 10:30 hrs. Pilot of 107 Squadron, 67 TAC/R Group reported and photographed an aluminum-colored cylinder ~12 ft long x 1 ft diameter floating in the air at 9,000 ft, suspended vertically with small fins and a mast projecting from the lower end. Pilot attacked the object; it partially deflated and a red flame without smoke resulted, but the cylinder did not disintegrate. Photos later proved unsuccessful (HQ IX TAC, 14 March 1945). ADI(K) Wing Commander Felkin (17 Feb 1945) suggested possible 'Flak Bombe' linkage to ADI(K) Report 562/1944 paragraphs 128-129.
outcome: Engaged with cannon; partial deflation, red flame without smoke; cylinder did not disintegrate

location_text: off west coast of Holland, 5155N/0355E
shape_raw: single jet propelled A/C employing probably rocket assists with tremendous reserve power
witness_role: USAF aircrews (307th Bomb Group, three crews)
summary: On 5 Sep 1948 at 1402Z, three 307th Bomb Group crews participating in Operation Daggar sighted an unidentified jet-propelled aircraft off the west coast of Holland (5155N/0355E) at 30,000 ft. Object was first observed cruising at normal jet speed on heading 120, then began leaving smoke and condensation trails accompanied by sudden acceleration and climb. Observers agreed it was a single jet, probably rocket-assisted, with tremendous reserve power exceeding 1947-vintage jets. Never within identification range. Evaluation B-2.
outcome: Object never approached within identification range; intent unknown.

location_text: Neubiberg Air Base, Germany
shape_raw: flying saucer observed hovering over Neubiberg Air Base for about thirty minutes
witness_role: USAF personnel at Neubiberg AB (per USAFE Item 14 memo)
summary: USAFE Item 14 (4 Nov 1948) reports that during the previous week one of the recurring 'flying saucers' was observed hovering over Neubiberg Air Base for approximately thirty minutes. Cited as part of a body of reports that USAFE intelligence officers concluded must be addressed beyond present intelligence framing.

location_text: unspecified lake in Sweden
shape_raw: flying saucer that crashed or landed in a lake; previously uncharted crater discovered on the lake floor
witness_role: Swedish technical expert (civilian, near home on edge of a lake)
summary: USAFE Item 14 relays a Swedish Air Intelligence-vetted account from a Swedish technical expert who, near his lakeside home, observed an object crash or land in the lake and carefully noted its azimuth from his position. A Swedish naval salvage team was deployed; divers reportedly discovered a previously uncharted crater on the lake floor not on current hydrographic charts, which Swedish intelligence assessed as caused by 'a flying saucer.' Final salvage results were promised but not yet available.
outcome: Salvage in progress at time of report; uncharted lakebed crater documented; final results pending.

location_text: United States — civilian witness report forwarded to AMC at Wright Field (specific location pending OCR)
shape_raw: flying disc / flying saucer (period terminology used in AF Form 112)

The bulk of 1949 incident filings in this folder are short citizen reports of disc-shaped objects observed in daylight or evening; per-incident date, location, and witness details require OCR of the scanned image pages.
outcome: Filed at AMC; many 1949 reports administratively closed under Project GRUDGE policy of conventional explanation.

location_text: United States — pilot report forwarded by AF unit to AMC (specific location pending OCR)
shape_raw: flying disc, daylight visual contact (per AF Form 112)
summary: Representative USAF pilot report from 1949 forwarded via AF Form 112 'Air Intelligence Information Report' channels to Air Materiel Command at Wright Field. 1949 saw a number of pilot disc sightings during the SIGN-to-GRUDGE transition that were investigated and filed in this 319.1 folder; per-incident specifics require OCR of the scanned image.
outcome: Filed at AMC under Project GRUDGE.

location_text: United States — civilian sighting routed via FBI / local police to AMC (specific location pending OCR)
shape_raw: flying saucer / flying disc (period terminology)

location_text: Detroit, Michigan — three blocks south of Six Mile at Lamphere Street
shape_raw: circular object with a crystal-type dome that reflected lights
summary: A 23-year-old Detroit civilian (former Civil Air Patrol) reported seeing a circular crystal-domed object reflecting lights, passing northward from the southwest over Detroit at 0408 local time on 17 April 1958.
outcome: FBI recommended forwarding report to USAF; witness's own attempt to call Selfridge Field was unsuccessful.

location_text: swamp area near Gut Alt Golssen, ~30 miles east of Berlin, Germany
shape_raw: circular in shape, 75 to 100 yards in diameter, and about 14 feet high, consisting of dark gray stationary top and bottom sections, five to six feet high. The approximate three foot middle section appeared to be a rapidly moving component producing a continuous blur similar to an aeroplane propeller
witness_role: Polish POW (forced laborer) at Gut Alt Golssen
summary: Krasuski (a Polish POW work-crew member) reported that on an unrecalled date in 1944, while cutting hay near Gut Alt Golssen, his crew's German tractor stalled twice when a high-pitched generator-like whine was present. After the first incident, while away from the road, he covertly observed a dark-gray circular craft 75-100 yards across and ~14 ft high rise vertically from a 50-ft tarpaulin-walled enclosure (100-150 yards diameter), clear the wall, and move slowly horizontally before being lost behind trees. Stationary top and bottom sections sandwiched a ~3 ft rapidly-rotating mid-section. SS guards secured the site. Tractor engine restarted normally only after the whining noise ceased.
outcome: Witness statement only; no further investigation noted in file

location_text: vicinity Mt. Rainier, Washington (state)
shape_raw: nine bright saucer-like objects flying in chain-like formation; later described as flat, disc-shaped
summary: Kenneth Arnold sighting near Mt. Rainier, Washington, 24 June 1947 — referenced via routing slips and press clippings appearing in early sections of FBI HQ file 62-HQ-83894. Arnold reported nine bright saucer-like craft moving in chain formation at high speed. The sighting coined the term 'flying saucer' and triggered the wave of reports the FBI logged through the summer of 1947. [Detail per OCR pending; sighting anchored on filename / case context.]
outcome: Triggered nationwide flying-disc wave; FBI briefly tasked to assist USAAF with collection.

location_text: United States — multiple field-office jurisdictions (1947 flying-disc wave)
shape_raw: flying disc / flying saucer (per period FBI teletype usage)
witness_role: civilian observers (multiple, reported to FBI field offices)
summary: Composite representative entry for the July 1947 wave of flying-disc reports forwarded by FBI field offices to Headquarters and filed in section 1 of 62-HQ-83894. Field offices teletyped citizen reports of flying discs to HQ following the Kenneth Arnold sighting; reports collected by FBI in cooperation with USAAF until the Bureau withdrew from collection later that year. [Per-incident specifics pending OCR.]
outcome: Forwarded to USAAF / Air Materiel Command; FBI cooperation withdrawn later in 1947.

location_text: United States (multiple jurisdictions)
shape_raw: flying saucer / flying disc (period terminology)
summary: Representative civilian flying-disc report logged in section 1 of 62-HQ-83894. Section 1 is dominated by 1947-era citizen letters and field-office teletypes forwarded to FBI HQ; per-incident date, location, and witness details require OCR of the scanned image pages. Held as case-file exhibit, no FBI investigative resolution recorded.
outcome: Filed as administrative-inquiry exhibit.

location_text: Codroy, Newfoundland (witnesses outside John Legge's store)
shape_raw: circle the size of a barrel head, bright red flame-color, with cone-shaped after-glow trail ~15 ft long
summary: Three Codroy, Newfoundland residents (John P. Legge, William Evans, Albert Samms) signed sworn statements at Harmon Field Intelligence Office on 17 July 1947 describing a bright red disc with cone-shaped after-glow heading northwest-to-east at approximately 6,000 ft for 15 seconds. Witnesses agreed it was much closer than a shooting star, much brighter than anything seen in the sky, and "definately was not" an aircraft on fire.
outcome: Statements forwarded to AAF intelligence.

location_text: Weather Bureau Airport Station, Richmond, Virginia
shape_raw: metallic chrome-shaped, like an ellipse with a flat level bottom and a dome-like round top
witness_role: U.S. Weather Bureau observers (Mr. Minczewski, Miss Baron) using theodolites during pilot-balloon observations
summary: WBAS Richmond observers tracked a strange metallic disc through theodolites during PIBAL pilot-balloon observations on three occasions over six months prior to July 1947. Last observation April 1947 11:00 EST (1100E pibal) showed the disc moving level east-to-west far north of station for 15 seconds when the balloon was at 15,000 ft; the disc appeared below the balloon yet was much larger in size in the instrument and shined like silver. Miss Baron observed it with her balloon at 27,000 ft; described as dull metallic luster.
weather: clear or very few clouds, good visibility
outcome: Memo from George A. Wright (WBAS) to Mr. Moxom (Weather Bureau Region 1).

location_text: Danforth, Illinois (farm field; reported via Sheriff Merle T. Wilmoth, Watseka, IL)
shape_raw: instrument with plaster-of-paris body, oval cavity, power microphone, copper-wire coils, magnetic metal piece — landed in farm field, burned 1.5-ft-diameter ash circle through 2.5-ft weeds
witness_role: civilian (farmer near Danforth, IL); package forwarded by Sheriff Merle T. Wilmoth, Watseka, IL
summary: An object dropped in a Danforth, Illinois farm field, burning a 1.5-ft-diameter circle in 2.5-ft weeds. Recovered "instrument" was forwarded to FBI by Sheriff Wilmoth and disassembled into: plaster-of-paris body, Nathaniel Baldwin Inc. power microphone (Salt Lake City; Pat May 10 1910 / Sept 14 1916, No 957403), small Polymat filter condenser, two bakelite cylinders wound with fine copper-wire coils, and a magnetic metal fragment. FBI radio section identified the components as old technology ("old stuff, or the coils were used quite some time ago").
outcome: FBI radio section identified the device as obsolete radio components, not a flying disc.

location_text: Skies above Durango, Mexico (city)
shape_raw: double truncated cone, joined at its bases, moves by something like jet propulsion and displaces itself by changing position
summary: Per a Mexico City newspaper clipping (16 March 1950) attached to FBI serial 220: National School of Engineering student German Horacio Robles Jr. claims to have photographed a flying saucer at 8,000-9,000 ft above Durango, Mexico. Object described as a double-truncated cone joined at its bases that moved by jet-like propulsion and changed position to redirect motive force, presenting different apparent forms. The student delivered both photos and his sketches of the device to the editorial offices.
outcome: Press report; FBI filed for reference

location_text: vicinity Norfolk, Virginia (Pan American DC-4 en route Miami)
shape_raw: 8 solid bodies of light, glowing orange-red like red-hot irons, ~100 ft diameter and 10-15 ft thick
witness_role: Pan American Airways aircrew (DC-4 captain William B. Nash and first officer William Fortenberry, both former Navy pilots)
summary: Pan Am DC-4 captain Nash and FO Fortenberry reported 8 disc-shaped objects, 100 ft diameter / 10-15 ft thick, glowing orange-red. Objects made a sharp 150-degree turn directly below the airliner, banked up at near 90 degrees as they gained altitude, were joined by two more identical craft, then their lights flickered off in succession at perhaps 10,000 ft. Pan Am ops manager Santos Ceyanes called them obviously not figments of imagination.
outcome: Reported to authorities; widely covered in press.

location_text: between Phillipsburg and Bradford, Pennsylvania (American Airlines DC-6 Newark-Detroit)
shape_raw: three bright whitish lights, looked like shining saucers
witness_role: American Airlines aircrew (Capt. Peter Killian, copilot John Dee), other crew, plus 25 passengers
summary: American Airlines Capt. Peter Killian (15 yrs experience) and copilot John Dee on Newark-Detroit nonstop reported three mysterious shining-saucer-like objects accompanying their DC-6 for 45 minutes between Phillipsburg and Bradford, PA at 8500 ft. Lost in haze on descent over Cleveland. Other crew and all 25 passengers also saw the objects.
outcome: Reported by AP wire.

location_text: vicinity Hanford Atomic Plant, Richlands, Washington
shape_raw: perfectly round disc, white in color, almost transparent, with small vapor trails like tentacles of an octopus; later became flat
witness_role: civilian aviators (4 Florida pilots, three of them WWII veterans; lead Capt. John Baldwin of Coral Gables, FL — 7,000 hrs)
summary: Four Florida pilots (Capt. John Baldwin lead, 7,000 hrs former USAF Pacific WWII) at 9,000 ft saw a perfectly round white, near-transparent disc 1,000-6,000 ft directly above them with octopus-tentacle-like vapor trails near the Hanford Engineering Works (atomic plant). The object was stationary then backed away, changed shape (became flat), gained speed and disappeared. Col. F.J. Clark, Hanford commanding officer, said saucer influx was unrelated to atomic operations.
outcome: Reported via United Press wire.

location_text: Vicinity Angoram, Papua New Guinea (approx. 4°S 144°E)
shape_raw: High-altitude, high-speed aircraft (radar return only); object not visually identified
witness_role: civilian airline pilot (Air Niugini, post-takeoff from Wewak en route Port Moresby)
summary: Air Niugini pilot's onboard radar picked up an aircraft flying south-to-north at high altitude and high speed while the airliner was over Angoram, PNG. Of the various PNG sightings on 24 Jan 1985, NIO placed the most credence in this radar-derived report.

location_text: Multiple points around Papua New Guinea (1900 local 24 Jan 1985)
shape_raw: Aircraft moving north-to-south, contrails visible (no shape detail)
summary: Multiple ground observers around PNG reported visual sighting of one aircraft moving north-to-south at 1900 local on 24 Jan 1985, with contrails. Reports characterized as fast-moving objects with lights, contrails and noise.

location_text: Multiple points around Papua New Guinea (2200 local 24 Jan 1985)
shape_raw: Six to eight aircraft traveling south to north, visible as contrails
summary: Multiple ground observers in PNG reported six to eight aircraft moving south-to-north at 2200 local on 24 Jan 1985, visible by contrails and accompanied by lights and noise.

location_text: Over Kazakhstan, 45°N 55°E (FL410)
shape_raw: Bright light of enormous intensity with bow-wave-like trail (shape indiscernible at night); resembled high-speed photo of bullet in flight
witness_role: civilian airline aircrew (Tajik Air B747SP — chief pilot and two colleagues, all American)
media_captured: Olympus pocket camera photos (per pilot, copies pending)
summary: Three American Tajik Air pilots flying a B747SP at FL410 over Kazakhstan watched a brilliant high-altitude object maneuver in circles, corkscrews and 90-degree high-G turns for ~40 minutes before adopting a horizontal high-speed course and disappearing over the horizon. Aircraft later flew under the object's contrails (estimated ~100,000 ft) whose paths matched the observed maneuvers. Captain photographed object with a pocket Olympus camera; crew rejected meteor hypothesis based on prior PanAm experience.
outcome: Object adopted horizontal high-speed course and disappeared over the horizon

Speed ~434 KTS (~499 mph), altitude FL200, trajectory W. Friendly aircraft at FL250 / 176 KTS. ~2 minute event, observer assessment Benign.

location_text: Lunar orbit (LM Intrepid AOT quadrant 1, dark side)
shape_raw: particles of light, flashes of light just seem to come from... sailing off in space
summary: While in lunar orbit aboard LM Intrepid, the LMP observed flashes / particles of light through the AOT in dark quadrant 1, coming from behind and sailing off into space. Initially considered as possibly water-boiler venting, but the LMP noted some appeared to escape the Moon and 'press off at the stars'.

location_text: translunar coast, shortly after S-IVB separation
shape_raw: very bright particles or fragments; jagged, angular, tumbling; flat flake-like particles, some ~6 inches across; 'looks like the Fourth of July'
summary: Shortly after S-IVB separation the Apollo 17 crew observed a large field of bright, jagged, angular, slowly tumbling fragments drifting past the windows; some described as flat flake-like particles up to 6 inches across, mostly moving away from the spacecraft. CMP photographed the field on Frame 70. Crew speculated the fragments might be ice chunks, peeling paint, or debris from the side of the S-IVB.
outcome: Assessed by crew as probable S-IVB-derived debris/ice/paint

location_text: translunar coast; object observed approximately 10-12 Earth diameters from spacecraft, ~45 degrees pitched up from spacecraft XZ plane
shape_raw: bright object, obviously rotating because it's flashing; rhythmic — one bright flash then a dull flash per rotation; two flashers
summary: On day 3 of translunar coast (~MET 02:18:42), CDR Cernan reported a bright physical object roughly 10-12 Earth diameters distant, rotating rhythmically and producing alternating bright and dull flashes (two flashers). Crew distinguished it from nearby particles and from stars, marked its position on the XZ axis at ~45 degrees pitch up, and Houston attempted to acquire it via gimbal angles. LMP later assessed it as probably the S-IVB booster's SLA panels reflecting sunlight.
outcome: LMP assessed object was likely the S-IVB / SLA panels; CDR initially stated 'something physical in the distance'

location_text: lunar surface, just north of Grimaldi crater (Oceanus Procellarum region)
shape_raw: a bright little flash right out there near that crater; a thin streak of light north of it
summary: From lunar orbit at MET ~03:15:38, LMP Schmitt reported observing a bright flash on the lunar surface just north of Grimaldi crater, followed by a thin streak of light. He suggested Houston check the seismometers for a small impact signature. Schmitt indicated he intended to keep looking for similar events as the spacecraft approached the edge of Mare Orientale.
outcome: LMP suggested cross-check with seismometers for an impact event

location_text: cislunar space, approximately 1 day from the Moon (Apollo 11 outbound)
shape_raw: appeared as a hollow cylinder, two connected rings, an open-book / open-suitcase / L shape; tumbling; 'it wasn't a cylinder'
summary: Apollo 11 crew (Armstrong, Aldrin, Collins) observed an unidentified sizable object out the window roughly 1 day from the Moon. Crew used monocular and sextant; appearance varied with sextant focus from L-shape/open-suitcase to two connected rings to a hollow cylinder seen end-on (Collins: 'you could look right down in its guts'). Crew checked with Mission Control; S-IVB was 6,000 miles away and could not be the source. Object was at the limit of eye resolution; size, range, and identity could not be determined. Crew was certain it wasn't a urine dump. Possible later candidate: Mylar from Lunar Module separation, but crew uncertain.
outcome: Not identified; possibly spacecraft-origin debris but unconfirmed

location_text: lunar orbit, looking toward Earth as it rose over lunar horizon (post-LM ascent CDH)
shape_raw: fairly bright light source
summary: From lunar orbit following ascent (CDH approach), as Earth came up above the lunar horizon, Aldrin observed what appeared to be a fairly bright light source on Earth — initially tentatively ascribed to a possible laser. Later, observing similar appearance from the CM approaching Earth, the crew revised the explanation to probable sunlight reflection off a smooth body of water (a lake). Aldrin still considered it 'an unusual phenomenon at that distance to see so bright a source of light.'
outcome: Initially candidate laser; later revised to probable lake reflection

location_text: Apollo 11 Command Module cabin, transearth coast
shape_raw: little flashes inside the cabin; sometimes single, sometimes double flashes ~1 ft apart, sometimes lines with no direction of motion; ~1 per minute average
summary: During transearth coast, Aldrin (and confirmed last day by Armstrong) observed light flashes inside the cabin spaced ~1 per minute on average. Single flashes, double flashes ~1 ft apart, and zero-velocity lines suggested 'some sort of penetration' of objects through the cabin. Aldrin and Armstrong surmised cosmic particles (neutron or atomic particle in the visible spectrum). Static electricity ruled out as full explanation.
outcome: Tentatively identified as cosmic-particle penetrations (now well-known cosmic-ray light flash phenomenon)

location_text: Apollo 17 transearth coast / lunar surface (cosmic ray light flashes); rendezvous window during re-entry
shape_raw: near-continuous light flashes when dark-adapted; one flash that appeared to be on the lunar surface
summary: Apollo 17 LMP Schmitt reported near-continuous brief light flashes visible to all three crewmembers while dark-adapted during translunar/transearth coast (the cosmic-ray phosphene phenomenon). Schmitt also recalled one flash he believed appeared on the lunar surface itself. Flashes ceased during the ALFMED blindfolded experiment interval and resumed afterward.
outcome: Phenomenon consistent with documented Apollo cosmic-ray-induced visual flashes.

location_text: Low Earth Orbit (Skylab wardroom window) — observed during SL-3 mission, ~1 week before splashdown
shape_raw: rather large red star; bright reddish object; never did take the shape of an object but always brighter than any other star or planet
summary: SL-3 astronauts Garriott, Bean, and Lousma tracked a bright reddish object out the wardroom window for approximately 10 minutes. Object had a ~10-second rotation period (brightness variation), drifted only 10-20 degrees during the 10-minute observation, and went into Earth shadow about 5-7 seconds after Skylab. Estimated within 30-50 nautical miles of Skylab. Crew never received an identification despite asking; never seen on subsequent orbits.
outcome: Never identified despite crew requests

location_text: Low Earth Orbit (Skylab) — during SL-4 mission
shape_raw: lights flashing outside with very a definite motion relative to ours
summary: SL-4 commander Carr reported the crew saw lights flashing outside the spacecraft on two or three occasions, with definite motion relative to Skylab. One or two appeared to be tumbling (oscillating light flashes). Crew presumed they were Skylab debris or other satellites and reported each sighting on dump tapes. Not identified.
outcome: Reported on air-to-ground; not identified

Object hovered, drifted east-to-west, then vanished after 5–10 seconds. The access gate had also unusually malfunctioned moments before the sighting.
outcome: Object disappeared; no media captured; witness reported the encounter to the FBI.

No vehicular EMI noted; witness experienced post-event sleep disturbance.
weather: Clear, good visibility, sun rising in east
outcome: Object vanished after light extinguished; could not be relocated

Then orbs flared down in reverse order until visual lost.

location_text: Western U.S.
shape_raw: orange 'mother' orbs launching/emitting smaller red orbs in groups of 2-4 (consensus 3); orange orb visible 1-2 seconds; red orbs travel horizontally, sometimes up at an angle, sometimes swooping down
summary: Across at least five recurrences over two dusks, three two-agent teams independently observed orange orbs that briefly appeared (1-2 seconds), launched groups of 2-4 red orbs, then disappeared. Red orbs generally moved away horizontally; some moved up at an angle or swooped down.

location_text: Western U.S., near rock pinnacle
shape_raw: glowing orange orb perched close to a rock pinnacle; like Eye of Sauron without the pupil; possible thin spindle connecting to rock; no sound
witness_role: federal law enforcement special agents (USPER5, USPER6)
summary: Two agents observed a glowing orange orb near a rock pinnacle; estimated 500-600 m range (AARO post-measurement: ~1050 m and 12-18 m diameter). Object hovered/suspended with zero resistance for about a minute. No noticeable sound.

location_text: Western U.S., restricted zone road
shape_raw: ill-defined dark kite shape with rounded sides; thin line from rear; later described to AARO as triangular; lights at ~2-3 ft off the ground (one red, one white) initially mistaken for a car
witness_role: federal law enforcement special agents (USPER5, USPER6)
summary: Two agents pursued what appeared to be a car on a road in a restricted zone. Object suddenly moved laterally off-road across desert at ~15-20 mph without altering orientation or altitude, with 'zero resistance'. Stopped 100 m off road, lights off, leaving a thin horizontal line in NVGs (~4 ft wide). Later described to AARO as triangular.

location_text: Western U.S., within a few hundred meters of the 'Dark Kite' sighting
shape_raw: kite-shaped object canted from lower right to upper left; lighting pattern similar to Dark Kite; appeared partially transparent (stars visible through it in NVG); ~6 m off the ground, drifting with the wind
witness_role: federal law enforcement special agents (USPER5, USPER6); USPER7 present but did not see object
summary: Approximately 30 minutes after the Dark Kite event and within a few hundred meters of the same area, USPER5 (NVG) and USPER6 (bare eye) observed a kite-shaped object ~6 m above ground, canted lower-right to upper-left, drifting slowly with the wind. Through NVG the object appeared partially transparent (stars visible through it). After visual loss, a spotlight beam appeared to be blocked at a localized spot in mid-air, then unblocked when redirected. USPER7 did not see the object.
outcome: team unable to reacquire
